import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 313

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/313](https://www.erdosproblems.com/313)
- [A54377](https://oeis.org/A54377) (Primary pseudoperfect numbers)
-/

namespace Erdos313

/--
This set contains all solutions `(m, P)` to the Erdős problem 313.
A solution is a pair where `m` is an integer `≥ 2` and `P` is a non-empty, finite set of
distinct prime numbers, such that the sum of the reciprocals of the primes in `P` equals `1 - 1/m`.
-/
def erdos313Solutions : Set (ℕ × Finset ℕ) :=
  {(m, P) | 2 ≤ m ∧ P.Nonempty ∧ (∀ p ∈ P, p.Prime) ∧ ∑ p ∈ P, (1 : ℚ) / p = 1 - 1 / m}

/--
Are there infinitely many pairs `(m, P)` where `m ≥ 2` is an integer
and `P` is a set of distinct primes such that the following equation holds:
$\sum_{p \in P} \frac{1}{p} = 1 - \frac{1}{m}$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_313 : answer(sorry) ↔ erdos313Solutions.Infinite := by
  sorry

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_313.variants.solution_6_2_3 : (6, {2, 3}) ∈ erdos313Solutions := by
  norm_num [erdos313Solutions]

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_313.variants.solution_42_2_3_7 : (42, {2, 3, 7}) ∈ erdos313Solutions := by
  norm_num [erdos313Solutions]

/--
An integer `n` is a **primary pseudoperfect number** if it is the denominator `m` in a
solution `(m, P)` to the Erdős 313 problem.
-/
def IsPrimaryPseudoperfect (n : ℕ) : Prop := ∃ P, (n, P) ∈ erdos313Solutions

/--
It is conjectured that the set of primary pseudoperfect numbers is infinite.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_313.variants.primary_pseudoperfect_are_infinite :
    Set.Infinite {n | IsPrimaryPseudoperfect n} := by
  sorry

/--
There are at least 8 primary pseudoperfect numbers. The first eight terms of
[A54377](https://oeis.org/A54377) are exhibited together with their explicit
prime decompositions.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_313.variants.exists_at_least_eight_primary_pseudoperfect :
    8 ≤ (Set.encard {n | IsPrimaryPseudoperfect n}) := by
  let S : Finset ℕ :=
    {2, 6, 42, 1806, 47058, 2214502422, 52495396602,
      8490421583559688410706771261086}
  have hS : (↑S : Set ℕ) ⊆ {n | IsPrimaryPseudoperfect n} := by
    intro x hx
    simp only [S, Finset.coe_insert, Finset.coe_singleton, Set.mem_insert_iff,
      Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hx
    rcases hx with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl
    · exact ⟨{2}, by norm_num [erdos313Solutions]⟩
    · exact ⟨{2, 3}, by norm_num [erdos313Solutions]⟩
    · exact ⟨{2, 3, 7}, by norm_num [erdos313Solutions]⟩
    · exact ⟨{2, 3, 7, 43}, by norm_num [erdos313Solutions]⟩
    · exact ⟨{2, 3, 11, 23, 31}, by norm_num [erdos313Solutions]⟩
    · exact ⟨{2, 3, 11, 23, 31, 47059}, by norm_num [erdos313Solutions]⟩
    · exact ⟨{2, 3, 11, 17, 101, 149, 3109}, by norm_num [erdos313Solutions]⟩
    · exact ⟨{2, 3, 11, 23, 31, 47059, 2217342227, 1729101023519}, by
        refine ⟨by decide, by decide, ?_, ?_⟩
        · intro p hp
          fin_cases hp <;> native_decide
        · native_decide⟩
  calc (8 : ℕ∞)
      = ((S.card : ℕ) : ℕ∞) := by decide
    _ = (↑S : Set ℕ).encard := (Set.encard_coe_eq_coe_finsetCard S).symm
    _ ≤ Set.encard {n | IsPrimaryPseudoperfect n} := Set.encard_le_encard hS

end Erdos313

findings.description: The docstring at lines 69–71 says the witnesses are the “first eight terms” of OEIS A054377. They are not: the witness set includes 8490421583559688410706771261086 but omits the smaller primary pseudoperfect number 5998279018951962402, now listed as a(8). All eight displayed witnesses and the formal lower bound remain correct. I independently verified the omitted number’s membership and the strict ordering in Lean.
findings.source_evidence: https://oeis.org/A054377/internal lists 2,6,42,1806,47058,2214502422,52495396602,5998279018951962402 and credits “a(8) from Pedro Martins, Apr 13 2026.” Han Wang, arXiv:2605.21518v1, §9, gives 5998279018951962402 = 2·3·11·17·101·157·1979·10093·16879 and verifies the primary pseudoperfect equation.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace “The first eight terms of [A54377] are exhibited” with “Eight primary pseudoperfect numbers are exhibited.” The theorem statement, witnesses, and category need not change.

reformulations.difference: The definition existentially chooses an arbitrary finite set of primes satisfying the reciprocal equation, whereas OEIS defines primary pseudoperfect numbers using precisely the prime divisors of n.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Let Q be the product of the chosen primes and A = Σ_{p∈P} Q/p. For every p∈P, A ≡ Q/p ≠ 0 modulo p, so gcd(A,Q)=1. The equation A/Q=(n−1)/n therefore forces n=Q by uniqueness of reduced denominators, and consequently P=n.primeFactors. Conversely, for an OEIS primary pseudoperfect number n>1, taking P=n.primeFactors supplies the required nonempty prime set. Proved the defining ↔, P=n.primeFactors, and n=∏p∈P,p in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean without sorry.

reformulations.difference: This variant counts qualifying integers rather than solution pairs (m,P).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Projection (m,P)↦m is injective on erdos313Solutions because every solution has P=m.primeFactors. Its image is exactly {n | IsPrimaryPseudoperfect n}. Thus infinitude of the solution set is equivalent to infinitude of the qualifying integers. Proved this ↔ in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean without sorry.

review.notes: All seven declarations were checked; no statement-level misformalizations were found. Both infinitude statements remain open according to the sources; Wang’s infinitude result is explicitly conditional. The eight-witness lower bound remains valid despite additional known examples. Lean checks covered all eight witnesses, exact rational arithmetic, zero/one and empty-set boundaries, and redundancy of the nonempty-set requirement. Artifacts are in /workspace/review/{scratch,equivalence,examples,new_eighth}.lean. Erdős Problems and OEIS were read through r.jina.ai after direct requests were Cloudflare-blocked. The reviewed file matches the requested commit byte-for-byte.
